title: annona pygmaea
intro: Annona pygmaea, commonly known as the small custard apple, is a species of flowering plant in the family Annonaceae. It has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, including the treatment of fever, cough, and respiratory issues, due to its antipyretic, anti-inflammatory, and expectorant properties. The therapeutic actions of Annona pygmaea are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including alkaloids, glycosides, and terpenoids, which have been shown to possess antioxidant, antimicrobial, and antitumor activities. The bioactive constituents of Annona pygmaea also include annonin, a compound with potential anticancer and neuroprotective effects.
